sections.en: Silver is changing hands near $60.83, -0.06% over the past 24 hours and -5.31% on a 7-day view. Spot trades below the 50-day average ($63.88) and below the 200-day average ($67.26), keeping the medium-term structure defensive. The 30-day tape reads as a drawdown phase (-11.24%), suggesting the market is still digesting supply.

sections.en:
**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is fully inverted (price < EMA20 < EMA50 < EMA200), the classic bear-stack in which rallies into value tend to be sold. Spot at $60.83 versus EMA20 $62.82, EMA50 $63.88 and EMA200 $67.26 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $60.72 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $58.78 as the 2σ downside envelope; first resistance at $60.87 (recent swing high); upper band $68.02 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $1.450 implies a typical daily range of roughly 2.4 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 40.7 — neutral territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits below its signal line (-1.22 vs -0.7832, histogram -0.4369), consistent with fading momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 38%; the 20-day band spans 15% of the mid — compressed, which often precedes a volatility expansion; 7-day turnover runs at 0.57x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned -11.24% over 30 days and -19.58% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (-5.31%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en:
**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires acceptance above $60.87 on expanding turnover. Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $60.72; failed reclaims of the 50-day average ($63.88). In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on Silver: spot $60.83 with the medium-term bias defensive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (-0.06%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
